title: Automated fat measurements associate with prostate therapy survival
summary: Deep-learning body segmentation measured fat compartments on routine PET/CT in 86 men receiving PSMA radioligand therapy. A higher intramuscular-fat proportion was associated with shorter overall survival, with volumetric measurements adding information beyond a single lumbar slice in the same cohort. This retrospective association does not establish a causal effect of fat, independent prediction or improved treatment selection.
ai_technology: Body and Organ Analysis; deep-learning CT segmentation
organization: University Hospital Münster; University of Münster; West German Cancer Centre

source_review.scope: Primary relevant model Methods, Results and limitations; exact primary identity and current primary PubMed correction/retraction relationships checked.

evidence.tested: Clinical overall-survival associations of automated three-dimensional and single-slice fat measurements, with multivariable analysis in 86 treated patients.
evidence.unknown: Independent validation and clinical decision benefit remain unestablished; selection, limited sample size and model fitting/evaluation in the same cohort can produce optimistic estimates.
evidence.ai_role: The pretrained BOA segmentation framework delineates body compartments to derive volumetric fat fractions for clinical survival-association analysis.
